paragraphs.text: **First-order driver.** The rally was driven by evidence that Apple could grow strongly without rapid unit expansion. Revenue, EPS and guidance all beat expectations. The iPhone unit number was modest, but the much higher ASP showed that the premium strategy—particularly the iPhone X—was lifting economics per user. Services growth added a recurring-revenue component, and upbeat guidance reduced concerns that the strong quarter was temporary.

**Second-order driver: expectations versus headline numbers.** Across these quarters, the market repeatedly reacted more strongly to revenue guidance, iPhone units, ASP/mix, Services growth and the implied trajectory of the next product cycle than to the reported EPS figure alone. A technical beat can therefore disappoint if the forward hurdle is higher; a year-over-year decline can rally if deterioration is smaller than feared.

**Third-order driver: evolution of the Apple narrative.** Over 2016–2018 the market's framing shifted from “Can the iPhone franchise grow again?” toward “Can Apple monetize a very large installed base through premium mix, Services, Wearables and capital returns?” That changes which metrics receive the greatest informational weight.
